children: Regulators set new guidelines warning automakers to refrain from disruptive competition abroad. Yet they look toothless for giants like $113 bln BYD and Geely, which both more than doubled August exports. A sales slump at home pushes Chinese firms to charge ahead at full speed.
Full view will be published shortly.
Follow Katrina Hamlin on Bluesky and Linkedin.

Chinese regulators on September 1 issued new guidelines for automakers' overseas operations, ​calling on companies to comply with laws governing outbound investment and overseas business activities, while strengthening anti-monopoly, anti-corruption and social responsibility compliance.
The notice was issued by the Ministry of Commerce, the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, and the State Administration for Market Regulation.
